subject: Renewal: Reserved GPU sizing & throughput for new model mix (context 128k + reranker)
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finexa.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@finexa.com
Date: Wed, 4 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal + capacity planning: larger model & reranker add-on

Hi Marissa / Hannah,

We’re starting renewal conversations for our Dedicated cluster that’s up in April. Over the last quarter we rolled a new larger customer-facing model (model: finexa-turbo-13B-longctx) and added a separate reranker stage that runs after candidate generation. Early results look promising, but the change in model mix is driving significantly more GPU memory and latency pressure than our original sizing assumed.

Current ask: we need to understand options for increasing reserved GPU capacity for the next 12 months (term change at renewal), and getting throughput guarantees during business hours. Concretely:
- Support for 128k context for session-based diagnostics (about 8–12% of production traffic).
- Reranker: synchronous reranker call that has tighter p99 latency SLAs.
- An elastic burst pool for periodic spikes (monthly reporting jobs + product launches).

Can you share recommended reserved pool sizing (GPU types), expected throughput improvements and an uplifted cost estimate? We can share usage exports on request.

Appreciate a quick readout this week if possible — our procurement window is the week of Feb 16.

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Head of AI Platforms | Finexa Health

Attachment: finexa_usage_q4_2025.csv (exported token/req breakdown)
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finexa.com>, Tom Roper <tom.roper@finexa.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity planning: larger model & reranker add-on

Hi Olivia — thanks for the heads up and for sending the export. I reviewed the CSV quickly and looped in Jordan (inference sizing) and Hannah (CS lead / renewal).

Quick proposals up front so you have something to react to before we schedule a call:
1) Reserved pool baseline: add 4x A100-80GB equivalents (or 6x A10G-equivalents if lower-cost) to the existing Dedicated pool to handle the 128k sessions plus reranker traffic.
2) Reranker: recommend running reranker on a smaller, low-latency group (2x A100-80GB) pinned to p99 < 300ms for the reranker flow; we can route reranker traffic to the pinned pool.
3) Burst pool: keep 2x pre-warmed burst nodes for seasonal spikes with autoscale to 6x for 2 hour windows; billed as burst capacity (metered).
4) SLA & throughput guarantees: propose a 99.9% availability + per-route throughput SLO for business hours (8am–6pm PST) with credits for sustained miss beyond agreed thresholds.

I’m attaching a draft SOW and a mutual action plan that lays out milestones and billing impact. Can we do a 30m call tomorrow (Friday Feb 6) to go over numbers and align on the procurement deadline?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_proposed_sow_v3.pdf, mutual_action_plan_finexa.xlsx
From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 6 Feb 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity planning: larger model & reranker add-on

Marissa / Olivia — did a quick sizing sketch based on the finexa_usage_q4_2025.csv and the model characteristics you shared. High level notes:
- finexa-turbo-13B-longctx at 128k context increases memory working set ~2.5x vs your previous 32k runs; throughput per GPU drops accordingly.
- Candidate generation (13B) can be batched aggressively; we estimate ~75 tok/sec per A100-80GB for typical mix when batched to 16.
- Reranker (smaller encoder model) is latency-sensitive; single-request p99 achievable on A100-80GB at ~220ms with optimized kernels.

Sizing options (cost/latency tradeoffs):
A) Conservative (recommended for safety): +4 A100-80GB reserved, +2 A100 pinned for reranker, burst pool autoscale 2->6. Expected headroom for growth + ~15% sustained throughput.
B) Cost-opt (balanced): +6 A10G-equivalent reserved (lower-memory), reranker on 2x A10G with tight co-location; expect slightly higher p99 for reranker but lower cost.

Operational notes: prefix KV caching for long-context sessions will recover ~20% of tokens for repeat contexts — we should include a caching policy in the MAP. Also recommend a staged rollout of the 128k traffic to validate NVMe-backed KV cache performance.

Drive doc with microbenchmarks: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Finexa-Retention-Docs

-Jordan
Principal Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed SOW & mutual action plan for Dedicated expansion (RDW-6791)

Hi Olivia / Tom — following our call last Friday, please find attached a proposed SOW and a Mutual Action Plan. Key items summarized below:

Term and capacity
- Term: 12 month renewal starting 2026-04-01.
- Reserved GPUs: 4x A100-80GB reserved capacity added to the Dedicated pool (baseline), 2x A100 pinned for reranker. Option to select 6x A10G as alternate sizing.

Throughput & SLA
- Business hours throughput guarantee: 95% of peak traffic served within agreed per-route throughput; reranker p99 target <= 300ms.
- Availability SLA: 99.9% for reserved pool. Credits: 5% of monthly reserved invoice per 1 hour of sustained SLA violation beyond threshold, up to 50%.

Bursting and operations
- Burst pool available on-demand with 15 min warm-up; pre-warmed nodes included for 2 scheduled events per quarter.
- Rollout plan includes KV caching config and an observability checklist (per-route tracing + token-level cost).

Commercials
- Uplift for reserved capacity: +32% on the existing Dedicated committed spend (detailed in attached SOW).
- DocuSign link to approve updated SOW: https://docusign.com/envelope/example12345

Next steps: please review and confirm in-principle by Feb 16 so procurement can approve the payment schedule. If you’re comfortable, we can send a redline-friendly copy of the SOW for procurement to route.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0131
From: Tom Roper <tom.roper@finexa.com>

Cc: procurement@finexa.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 13:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed SOW & mutual action plan for Dedicated expansion (RDW-6791)

Marissa — thank you, this reads clean. A few quick asks before we sign: 
1) Can you add a clause that provides a limited SLA credit if we hit a sustained throughput regression during the staged rollout (first 30 days)? We’re sensitive to production regressions while we flip traffic to 128k contexts.
2) For the reranker pool, can you commit to p99 < 300ms during business hours or is that best-effort? If it’s a SLO we’ll need remediation terms.
3) Is the burst pool price metered separately or part of the reserved uplift? We want to model monthly cost variability for finance.

Assuming answers to those three, we’re prepared to move to signature and will route the SOW through procurement. Also: can you add one additional pre-warmed node to the burst pool for a small margin?

Regards,
Tom Roper
VP Platform Engineering | Finexa Health
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: Tom Roper <tom.roper@finexa.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finexa.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, procurement@finexa.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed SOW & mutual action plan for Dedicated expansion (RDW-6791)

Tom — great questions. Short answers:
1) Rollout regression credit: yes, we can add a 30-day staged-rollout protection clause in the SOW that provides a limited credit (2% of monthly reserved fee) if throughput regressions caused by the rollout exceed agreed thresholds. We’ll include the exact trigger and measurement method in the MAP.
2) Reranker p99: we can include the p99 <= 300ms as a per-route SLO during business hours. Remediation: operational runbook + 50% billing credit for sustained misses (windowed, capped).
3) Burst pool billing: metered separately from reserved uplift; monthly reports will show burst usage and charges. We’ll add 1 extra pre-warmed node as requested.

I’ll circulate an updated SOW with those clauses redlined by EOD. Proposed next step: procurement points the SOW to their signature flow and we target 2026-03-01 as DocuSign completion to allow for April 1 start.

Thanks,
Marissa
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
